speaker: PROFESSOR
text: Let's recap the journey we've taken today. We started with a paradox. Robots can do backflips but can't fold laundry. Classical robotics gave us beautiful equations but couldn't handle the messiness of the real world.

speaker: PROFESSOR
text: Reinforcement learning promised to learn from experience, but it's dangerous, data-hungry, and struggles with complex rewards. Imitation learning showed us how to learn from human demonstrations safely and efficiently.

speaker: PROFESSOR
text: But naive imitation fails on multimodal tasks. The mode averaging problem destroys coherent behavior. The solution? Output distributions, not point estimates. Use deep generative modeling to sample coherent actions.

speaker: PROFESSOR
text: And this isn't science fiction. Companies like Physical Intelligence are already deploying these techniques. Foundation models are emerging that you can fine-tune for your own tasks.

speaker: PROFESSOR
text: Over the next three lessons, you'll learn to build these systems yourself. VAEs, action chunking, transformer architectures. By the end, you'll train your SO-ARM101 to fold clothes using the same techniques powering the most advanced robots in the world.

speaker: PROFESSOR
text: The future of robotics is not locked in corporate labs. It's accessible to anyone willing to learn. And that journey starts now.
